note: Reel 30: How Sure Are You? Script v3, after two reviews of v1 and the cold reader's note that the officer's 'Good' reads as an obvious trick. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart); the officer is am_michael (audition, 10 Nov: no creak on either line). Facts: docs/research.md.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: This time, he's one of these six, and whoever you pick goes to prison.
Out of ten, how sure are you?
He's a drawing, so he can't see what you picked.
Of course it is. Look at him.
And whoever you picked is still going to prison.
You still know how sure you were, because I asked.
If nobody asks, one good and you'd swear you were sure from the start.
In America, police told a real witness she'd picked the same man again, and she thought,
It was the wrong man, and Ronald Cotton lost more than ten years.
lines.text_kokoro: It was the wrong man, and Ronald [Cotton](/kˈɑːtən/) lost more than ten years.

lines.text: He really is one of these six.
I could tell you which, but you'd believe me.
